title: Yamal Reveals Messi's Words After World Cup Final Embrace
excerpt: The 19-year-old said the Argentine icon told him to 'keep following my path' after Spain's victory, calling the advice worth as much as his winner's medal.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Lamine Yamal received advice from Messi to 'keep following my path' after Spain's World Cup victory.
  • Yamal is the first player to win both the European Championship and World Cup before turning 20.
  • Messi scored eight goals and four assists in the tournament but lost in his likely final international match.
  • Messi expressed immense pain after the loss, stating it will take time to heal.
  • Yamal's rise parallels Messi's, both emerging from Barcelona's La Masia academy as teenage talents.

Lamine Yamal has revealed what Lionel Messi told him in their embrace after Spain's victory over Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final, describing the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner's words as meaning “as much as the gold medal hanging around my neck.”

The 19-year-old Barcelona forward, who helped Spain claim their second World Cup title with a dominant display at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday, made a beeline for the crestfallen Messi after the final whistle and helped the Argentine icon to his feet before the pair exchanged words that have now gone public.

A Passing of the Torch

Speaking at a press conference on Monday, Yamal described the post-match moment with the player he grew up idolising.

“He's the greatest player in history and someone I've always looked up to. After the match, I wanted to show him my respect. He told me to keep following my path and that the future belongs to our generation.”

— Lamine Yamal

“If someone had told me a few years ago that I'd be here lifting the World Cup after playing against Lionel Messi, I would have thought they were crazy,” Yamal added.

The image of their embrace instantly circled the globe, echoing a famous photograph from 2007 in which a five-month-old Yamal was held by Messi during a charity photoshoot at Barcelona. Messi had reflected on that photo before the final during an appearance at Fanatics Fest in New York, calling it “crazy” and adding: “I took a photo with him while he was a baby and today we are both facing each other in the World Cup.”

Messi's Last Dance

Messi, 39, was extraordinary throughout the tournament, scoring eight goals and registering four assists as Argentina reached a second consecutive final. But his brilliance was not enough to overcome a Spanish side that conceded just one goal in the entire competition, with goalkeeper Unai Simón recording a tournament-record six clean sheets.

Cameras captured a heartbroken Messi sitting on the MetLife Stadium turf after the final whistle, seemingly avoiding the post-match fracas that erupted around him. Nicolas Otamendi confronted Rodri, Leandro Paredes threw Gavi to the ground, and an Argentine coaching staff member was reported to have struck Dani Olmo.

Almost 24 hours later, Messi issued a statement on social media: “The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal. But I also hold onto all the good things.” He added that reaching two consecutive World Cup finals was an achievement the squad should be proud of, and congratulated Spain on their triumph.

A Generational Talent Arrives

Yamal's World Cup victory completes a remarkable rise that has drawn inevitable comparisons to Messi. Both emerged from Barcelona's La Masia academy as teenage prodigies. Both play with a similarly mesmerising low centre of gravity and left-footed dribbling style. But Yamal has now achieved something Messi did not at his age: winning football's two biggest international trophies before turning 20.

Having lifted the European Championship with Spain in 2024 at age 16, Yamal joined an exclusive list of players who started and won a World Cup final before their 20th birthday — a group that includes Pelé, Giuseppe Bergomi and Kylian Mbappé.

Whether Messi has played his final international match remains officially unconfirmed. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni deflected questions about it. But the scene at MetLife Stadium — the greatest of all time sitting on the turf, his heir helping him up and inheriting his blessing — had the unmistakable feel of a coronation.
